## Source: amazon-inspector (422359e6c8044efa7c3873ff0859acb1480ea95413cbfb8829dc4c674de6f8d5)
bigops-offers@35.6.8 executes a binary dropper at require time. index.js loads./_init on import; _init.js assembles C2 hostnames from split string arrays (workers.dev subdomains oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev) and fetches a platform-specific binary via https.get. A DNS TXT-record fallback assembles base64 payload chunks from c.dl.wel1.ru and 0..N.dl.wel1.ru (sdk/ext/pkg/net subdomains). The retrieved bytes are written to a disguised path (dotnet_diag_<rand>.exe on Windows,.cache_<rand> on Unix), chmod 0o755, and spawned detached via /bin/sh or cmd. A.analytics_state lock file and DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK env checks provide a telemetry cover story. Destinations, filenames, and delivery channels are string-split to evade static detection.

## Source: ghsa-malware (7510590b844279a07c74814147bbd492c9b47b7addfe9c78bcb13c5c6edc1ac4)
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised. All secrets and keys stored on that computer should be rotated immediately from a different computer. The package should be removed, but as full control of the computer may have been given to an outside entity, there is no guarantee that removing the package will remove all malicious software resulting from installing it.
